name: Deficiency of both the Kidney Yin and Yang
description: Deficiency of both the Kidney Yin and Yang (Shèn Yīn Yáng Liǎng Xū, 肾阴阳两虚) is a empty TCM pattern. Key signs: Lower back cold and aching, Feeling cold in the...

timing_worsening_explanation: Symptoms tend to worsen in the late afternoon and evening, corresponding to the Kidney's peak time on the organ clock (5-7 PM for the Kidneys). Night sweats and tidal heat often appear in the late afternoon or overnight. Early-morning diarrhoea (around 3-5 AM, sometimes called 'fifth-watch diarrhoea') can occur when Yang deficiency is prominent, as this is when Yang Qi is at its weakest. Cold symptoms are worse in winter, while the heat-type symptoms (flushing, night sweats) may be more noticeable in warmer seasons. Symptoms generally worsen with age and are often more pronounced during periods of stress or overwork.
practitioner_notes:
Diagnosing this pattern requires recognising the coexistence of two apparently contradictory sets of signs: cold symptoms from Yang deficiency and heat symptoms from Yin deficiency. The hallmark is a patient who feels both chilly (cold limbs, cold lower back, frequent pale urine at night) and intermittently hot (flushing, night sweats, dry mouth). This paradoxical presentation is the key diagnostic clue.
The underlying logic is that Yin and Yang within the Kidneys are deeply interdependent. Yin provides the material basis (fluids, Essence, cooling capacity) while Yang provides the warming, activating force. When one side has been deficient for a long time, it eventually depletes the other. For instance, if Kidney Yang has been weak for years and cannot properly transform and generate Yin fluids, Yin deficiency develops on top of the existing Yang deficiency. The reverse pathway is also possible. In either case, both the warming function and the nourishing reserves of the Kidneys are compromised.
Practitioners look at the overall balance to determine which side is more depleted. Key diagnostic anchors include the tongue (pale and puffy suggests Yang deficiency dominance; red and dry suggests Yin deficiency dominance) and the pulse at the Chi position. The presence of both cold and heat signs in the same patient, together with lower back soreness, dizziness, tinnitus, and deep fatigue, points strongly toward this dual-deficiency pattern. It is most commonly seen in elderly individuals, those with chronic illness, or after prolonged overwork.
pathophysiology: Both the warming (Yang) and the nourishing (Yin) functions of the Kidney are depleted, so the body simultaneously lacks internal warmth and internal moisture, producing a confusing mixture of cold and heat symptoms.
treatment_principle: Nourish Kidney Yin and warm Kidney Yang simultaneously, supplementing both Yin and Yang to restore the Kidney's foundational balance
typical_timeline: 3-6 months minimum for noticeable improvement; 6-12 months or longer for chronic or severe cases. Milder cases in younger patients may respond within 2-3 months.
formula_modifications:
If the person feels mainly cold with very cold limbs and a weak lower backThis indicates Yang deficiency is the dominant aspect. Increase the dosage of warming herbs such as Fu Zi (prepared aconite) and Rou Gui (cinnamon bark), or shift from Jin Gui Shen Qi Wan toward You Gui Wan. Add Du Zhong (eucommia bark) to strengthen the lower back.
If the person experiences more heat signs such as night sweats, hot palms and soles, and dry mouthThis indicates Yin deficiency is more prominent. Emphasise Yin-nourishing herbs and consider using Zuo Gui Wan as the base formula. Add Zhi Mu (anemarrhena) and Huang Bai (phellodendron) to clear deficiency heat, or add Nü Zhen Zi (privet fruit) and Han Lian Cao (eclipta).
If the person also feels very tired with poor appetite and loose stoolsThis suggests the Spleen has also become weakened, which is common in long-standing Kidney deficiency. Add Huang Qi (astragalus), Dang Shen (codonopsis), and Bai Zhu (white atractylodes) to support digestive function, ensuring the body can actually absorb the nourishing herbs.
If there is noticeable fluid retention or swelling in the legsThe Kidney's ability to manage water metabolism is impaired. Add Fu Ling (poria) and Ze Xie (alisma) to promote gentle fluid drainage, or consider using Ji Sheng Shen Qi Wan (a modified version of Kidney Qi Pill with added diuretic herbs).
If there is significant lower back pain with weakness and sorenessAdd Du Zhong (eucommia), Xu Duan (teasel root), and Sang Ji Sheng (mulberry mistletoe) to strengthen the sinews, bones, and lower back specifically.
If a man experiences impotence or premature ejaculationAdd Lu Jiao Jiao (deer antler glue) and Yin Yang Huo (epimedium) to strengthen reproductive Yang, along with Suo Yang (cynomorium) and Tu Si Zi (dodder seed) to secure the Essence.
If a woman experiences irregular periods, scanty flow, or difficulty conceivingAdd Dang Gui (angelica root) to nourish Blood, and Xian Mao (curculigo) and Yin Yang Huo (epimedium) to warm the Kidney and regulate the Chong and Ren vessels. Er Xian Tang is especially suitable in this scenario.

causes_details: [{"cause_title": "Ageing and natural decline of Kidney Essence", "explanation": "In TCM, the Kidneys store 'Essence' (Jing), a fundamental substance that underpins growth, reproduction, and vitality. This Essence naturally declines with age. The Huang Di Nei Jing describes this in its famous passages about the seven-year and eight-year life cycles for women and men respectively. As Essence dwindles, both the Yin (the cooling, moistening, nourishing aspect) and the Yang (the warming, activating, transforming aspect) of the Kidney gradually weaken. In many people, one side declines first and eventually drags the other down with it, because Yin and Yang are interdependent. This natural decline is the single most common cause of Kidney Yin-Yang dual deficiency."}, {"cause_title": "Prolonged Kidney Yin Deficiency damaging Yang (Yin damaging Yang)", "explanation": "When Kidney Yin is depleted for a long time without adequate treatment, the Kidney's material foundation becomes too weak to support and generate Yang. Think of it like a lamp running out of oil: the fuel (Yin) is gone, so the flame (Yang) inevitably gutters. The classical teaching is 'Yin damages and reaches Yang' (阴损及阳). Someone who started with signs like night sweats, dry throat, and heat in the palms gradually develops cold limbs, frequent pale urination, and fatigue as Yang also fails."}, {"cause_title": "Prolonged Kidney Yang Deficiency damaging Yin (Yang damaging Yin)", "explanation": "Conversely, long-standing Kidney Yang deficiency can erode Yin. When the warming, transforming function of Yang is too weak, the body cannot properly generate and circulate fluids and Essence. Without adequate warmth, Yin substances cannot be produced and replenished. This is described as 'Yang damages and reaches Yin' (阳损及阴). A person who initially suffered mainly from cold signs gradually develops dryness, thinning of fluids, and heat sensations mixed in with the cold."}, {"cause_title": "Overwork, exhaustion, and chronic stress", "explanation": "Sustained overwork, whether physical or mental, draws heavily on the Kidney's reserves. The Kidneys are considered the body's deepest energy reserve, and chronic overexertion depletes this reserve over time. Irregular sleep, working through the night (when Yin should be replenishing), and relentless stress all accelerate this drain. Eventually both the Yin and Yang aspects of the Kidney are consumed."}, {"cause_title": "Excessive sexual activity", "explanation": "In TCM, sexual activity directly uses Kidney Essence. Within reasonable limits this is normal and healthy. However, excessive sexual activity, especially when the body is already tired or unwell, drains Essence faster than it can be replenished. Since Essence is the material root of both Kidney Yin and Kidney Yang, over-depletion of Essence naturally leads to weakening of both."}, {"cause_title": "Chronic illness consuming the Kidneys", "explanation": "Any prolonged illness tends to eventually affect the Kidneys because they are the body's foundational reserve. Chronic disease consumes Qi, Blood, and Essence over time. As the classical saying goes, 'prolonged illness reaches the Kidneys.' Whether the original disease affects the Lungs, Spleen, Liver, or any other system, if it persists long enough, the Kidneys will be drawn upon and eventually depleted in both their Yin and Yang aspects."}, {"cause_title": "Constitutional weakness and inherited insufficiency", "explanation": "Some people are born with weaker Kidney Essence due to factors during conception or pregnancy, such as the parents' health being poor at the time, or the mother being malnourished or very stressed during pregnancy. This is called 'innate insufficiency' (先天不足). People with this constitution have less Kidney Essence to draw on throughout life and may develop Kidney Yin-Yang deficiency earlier than others."}]

formulas.name: You Gui Wan
formulas.description: Right-Restoring Pill from Zhang Jingyue's Jing Yue Quan Shu. This formula warms Kidney Yang and fills Essence using Fu Zi, Rou Gui, and Lu Jiao Jiao alongside Yin-nourishing Shu Di Huang, Shan Yao, and Gou Qi Zi. It embodies the principle of 'seeking Yang within Yin' and is preferred when Yang deficiency signs are more prominent.

formulas.name: Zuo Gui Wan
formulas.description: Left-Restoring Pill, also from Zhang Jingyue. This heavily Yin-nourishing formula uses Gui Ban Jiao and Lu Jiao Jiao as 'flesh and blood' substances to fill Essence powerfully. It is chosen when Yin deficiency signs predominate in the dual-deficiency picture, embodying 'seeking Yin within Yang'.

formulas.name: Er Xian Tang
formulas.description: Two Immortals Decoction. Combines Kidney-warming herbs (Xian Mao, Yin Yang Huo, Ba Ji Tian) with Yin-protecting herbs (Zhi Mu, Huang Bai) and Blood-nourishing Dang Gui. Originally designed for menopausal symptoms with Kidney Yin-Yang deficiency and upward-flaring deficiency Fire. Particularly useful when there is simultaneous chilling and hot flushes.

formulas.name: Gui Lu Er Xian Jiao
formulas.description: Tortoise Shell and Deer Antler Two-Immortal Glue. This classical formula uses four potent ingredients: Gui Ban (tortoise plastron), Lu Jiao (deer antler), Ren Shen (ginseng), and Gou Qi Zi. It powerfully replenishes both Yin Essence and Yang Essence using 'flesh and blood' substances, suitable for severe depletion of Kidney Yin and Yang.

formulas.name: Di Huang Yin Zi
formulas.description: Rehmannia Drink. This formula from Liu Hejian simultaneously nourishes Kidney Yin and warms Kidney Yang, using herbs like Shu Di Huang, Shan Zhu Yu, Rou Cong Rong, Ba Ji Tian, Fu Zi, and Rou Gui. It is classically indicated for severe Kidney Yin-Yang deficiency affecting speech and mobility.

herbs.name: Shu Di Huang
herbs.description: Prepared Rehmannia root (Shu Di Huang) is the chief herb for nourishing Kidney Yin and filling the Essence. It is warm in nature and richly nourishing, making it the cornerstone of most Kidney-tonifying formulas.

herbs.name: Shan Zhu Yu
herbs.description: Cornus fruit (Shan Zhu Yu) warms and nourishes both the Liver and the Kidney, and has an astringent quality that helps secure leaking Essence, reducing symptoms like sweating and seminal emission.

herbs.name: Shan Yao
herbs.description: Chinese yam (Shan Yao) gently tonifies both Qi and Yin of the Kidney and Spleen. It supports the digestive system so the body can absorb nourishing herbs more effectively.

herbs.name: Gou Qi Zi
herbs.description: Goji berry (Gou Qi Zi) nourishes the Liver and Kidney, replenishing Yin Essence and benefiting the eyes. Its mild warming tendency makes it suitable for patterns where both Yin and Yang are depleted.

herbs.name: Tu Si Zi
herbs.description: Dodder seed (Tu Si Zi) is neutral in temperature and tonifies both Kidney Yang and Kidney Yin Essence. It strengthens reproductive function and secures Essence without being overly heating or cooling.

herbs.name: Lai Fu Zi
herbs.description: Prepared aconite root (Fu Zi) powerfully warms Kidney Yang and rescues depleted Yang. It is used in small amounts when Yang deficiency signs predominate, but must be carefully balanced with Yin-nourishing herbs.

herbs.name: Rou Gui
herbs.description: Cinnamon bark (Rou Gui) warms the Kidney and fortifies Yang. It also has the important function of guiding Fire back to its source (the Kidney), which helps when deficiency heat floats upward.

herbs.name: Du Zhong
herbs.description: Eucommia bark (Du Zhong) tonifies the Liver and Kidney and strengthens the sinews and bones, directly addressing the low back and knee soreness that is a hallmark of this pattern.

herbs.name: Yin Yang Huo
herbs.description: Epimedium (Yin Yang Huo) warms Kidney Yang and strengthens tendons and bones. It is especially useful when sexual function is weakened, and pairs well with Yin-nourishing herbs in dual-deficiency patterns.

herbs.name: Ba Ji Tian
herbs.description: Morinda root (Ba Ji Tian) warms the Kidney Yang, strengthens tendons and bones, and disperses cold-dampness. It is gentler than Fu Zi and well-suited for long-term tonification of Kidney Yang.

acupoints.name: Guanyuan REN-4
acupoints.description: Guan Yuan (REN-4) is located on the lower abdomen, 3 cun below the navel. It is one of the body's most important points for tonifying both Kidney Yang and the original Qi. Moxa on this point warms the lower abdomen and powerfully reinforces the Kidney's foundational energy.

acupoints.name: Shenshu BL-23
acupoints.description: Shen Shu (BL-23) is the Back-Shu point of the Kidney, located beside the second lumbar vertebra. It directly tonifies Kidney Qi and benefits both Yin and Yang of the Kidney. It is an essential point in virtually all Kidney deficiency patterns.

acupoints.name: Taixi KI-3
acupoints.description: Tai Xi (KID-3) is the Source point of the Kidney channel, located between the inner ankle bone and the Achilles tendon. It primarily nourishes Kidney Yin but also has the ability to support Kidney Yang, making it ideal for dual deficiency patterns.

acupoints.name: Mingmen DU-4
acupoints.description: Ming Men (DU-4) is located on the spine between the second and third lumbar vertebrae. Known as the 'Gate of Vitality', it directly warms and reinforces Kidney Yang and the vital fire. Moxibustion here is particularly powerful for the Yang-deficient aspect of this pattern.

acupoints.name: Sanyinjiao SP-6
acupoints.description: San Yin Jiao (SP-6) is where the three Yin channels of the leg (Kidney, Liver, Spleen) meet. It nourishes Yin and Blood broadly, supports the Kidney, and regulates reproductive and urinary functions.

acupoints.name: Qihai REN-6
acupoints.description: Qi Hai (REN-6) is located 1.5 cun below the navel. It tonifies Qi and Yang broadly, and helps lift and consolidate the body's overall vitality when deeply depleted.

acupoints.name: Fuliu KI-7
acupoints.description: Fu Liu (KID-7) is the Metal (Jing-River) point of the Kidney channel, known for its strong ability to nourish Kidney Yin and regulate sweating. It is particularly useful when night sweats or spontaneous sweating are prominent.

classical_texts.source: Huang Di Nei Jing Su Wen (Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic, Basic Questions)
classical_texts.translation: The foundational theory of Kidney Yin and Yang, the storage of Essence, and the life-cycle decline of Kidney Qi are discussed throughout the Su Wen. The famous passages on the seven-year cycles for women and eight-year cycles for men describe how Kidney Qi naturally waxes and wanes with age, providing the theoretical basis for understanding age-related Kidney Yin-Yang depletion.

classical_texts.source: Jing Yue Quan Shu (Complete Works of Zhang Jingyue)
classical_texts.translation: Zhang Jingyue (Ming Dynasty) is perhaps the most important figure in the treatment of Kidney Yin-Yang deficiency. His work contains the Left-Restoring Pill (Zuo Gui Wan) and Right-Restoring Pill (You Gui Wan), along with their drink (Yin) versions. His famous principle that 'those who are skilled at nourishing Yang must seek Yang within Yin, and those skilled at nourishing Yin must seek Yin within Yang' (善补阳者必于阴中求阳,善补阴者必于阳中求阴) remains the guiding therapeutic principle for this pattern.

classical_texts.source: Jin Gui Yao Lue (Essential Prescriptions from the Golden Cabinet)
classical_texts.translation: Zhang Zhongjing's work contains Shen Qi Wan (Kidney Qi Pill), the ancestor formula for treating Kidney Yang deficiency with a Yin-nourishing base. This formula became the template for later Kidney Yin-Yang dual supplementation approaches.

classical_texts.source: Shang Han Lun (Treatise on Cold Damage)
classical_texts.translation: The Shao Yin disease chapter describes patterns of Kidney and Heart Yang-Yin depletion with cold limbs, desire to sleep, and a faint pulse, representing the most acute manifestation of Kidney Yin-Yang exhaustion in the context of febrile disease.

faqs.question: What is Deficiency of both the Kidney Yin and Yang in TCM?
faqs.answer: Both the warming (Yang) and the nourishing (Yin) functions of the Kidney are depleted, so the body simultaneously lacks internal warmth and internal moisture, producing a confusing mixture of cold and heat symptoms.

faqs.question: What are the key signs of Deficiency of both the Kidney Yin and Yang?
faqs.answer: Key signs include: Lower back cold and aching, Feeling cold in the limbs, Intermittent hot flushes or tidal heat, Night sweats, Dizziness, Ringing in the ears, Frequent nighttime urination, Reduced sex drive, Dry mouth and throat, Loose stools or early-morning diarrhoea, Weak and sore knees, Poor memory and forgetfulness, Thinning or greying hair.

faqs.question: What formulas treat Deficiency of both the Kidney Yin and Yang?
faqs.answer: Common formulas for Deficiency of both the Kidney Yin and Yang include: You Gui Wan, Zuo Gui Wan, Er Xian Tang, Gui Lu Er Xian Jiao, Di Huang Yin Zi.

faqs.question: What Western conditions relate to Deficiency of both the Kidney Yin and Yang?
faqs.answer: This pattern is associated with: Perimenopausal syndrome, Essential hypertension, Chronix glumerulonephritis, Chronic pyelonephritis, Polycystic kidneys, Renal vascular disease, Hyperthyroid, Urinary tract infection, Chronic kidney disease, Menopause (perimenopause and post-menopause), Hypothyroidism, Adrenal insufficiency, Male hypogonadism, Osteoporosis, Chronic fatigue syndrome, Infertility (male and female), Diabetes mellitus (type 2), Premature ovarian insufficiency, Aplastic anaemia, Chronic low back pain.

faqs.question: What is the treatment principle for Deficiency of both the Kidney Yin and Yang?
faqs.answer: Nourish Kidney Yin and warm Kidney Yang simultaneously, supplementing both Yin and Yang to restore the Kidney's foundational balance
